takeaway: Gilmore's groin (sportsman's hernia): chronic groin pain after sport, worse with sudden twisting movements, usually without a lump.

lines.text: A twenty-eight-year-old man has abdominal and groin pain after a rugby match.
The book explains this as Gilmore's groin, the sportsman's hernia, also called athletic pubalgia.
It is a syndrome of groin disruption: chronic pain, made worse by sudden and twisting movements.
In general, there is no associated lump.
Compare the other patients: the plumber with a reducible groin swelling has an inguinal hernia,
the woman with a lump in her upper thigh has a femoral hernia, and a lump at an old scar is an incisional hernia.
So the correct pairing is the rugby player with groin pain after the match.
